title: Reactions that release or absorb heat
keyIdea: Exothermic reactions give energy out (temperature rises); endothermic reactions take energy in (temperature falls).

kid: Some reactions give out heat. They are called exothermic, and the mixture gets warmer. Burning is exothermic.
Some reactions take in heat. They are called endothermic, and the mixture gets colder. Sherbet fizzing on your tongue feels cool because it takes in heat.
adult: Exothermic: energy goes out to the surroundings, so the temperature rises. The products have less energy than the reactants. Examples: burning, neutralisation, hand warmers.

Endothermic: energy is taken in, so the temperature falls. The products have more energy. Examples: heating limestone, photosynthesis and cold packs. Every reaction needs some energy to start. That is the hump on the energy profile.

familyTip: Feel a hand warmer, then a cold pack. Which gives energy to your hand, and which takes it away?

practice.prompt: The temperature rises from 20 °C to 31 °C. The reaction is…
practice.explain: It got warmer, so energy was given out: exothermic.

practice.prompt: A reaction starts at {a} °C and ends at {=a+d} °C. By how many degrees did it warm up?
The temperature falls from {a} °C to {=a-d} °C. By how many degrees did it fall?

choices: Heating limestone to break it down
practice.hint: Which one needs heat put in all the time?

pool.prompt: In an exothermic reaction the products have…
pool.explain: Energy left, so the products have less.

pool.prompt: A hand warmer uses a reaction that is…
The reactants have {a} kJ of energy and the products have {=a-d} kJ. How much energy is given out, in kJ?
A cold pack drops from {a} °C to {b} °C. How many degrees did it fall?

choices: The energy needed to start a reaction
The energy given out at the end
pool.explain: It is the energy needed to get the reaction going.

pool.prompt: Why does sherbet feel cold on your tongue?
choices: Its reaction takes in heat from your tongue
It is kept in a freezer
pool.explain: The fizzing reaction is endothermic, so it takes in heat.

pool.prompt: On the energy profile of an endothermic reaction, the products are…
pool.explain: They have gained energy, so they sit higher.

visual.caption: Drag the products' energy level up or down. Watch what happens to the temperature of the surroundings.

lab.caption: Mix acid and alkali with universal indicator. Watch the colour, temperature and bubbles, then test the gas.
